title: From the surge-margin example to an uncertainty-aware anti-surge controller
author: DanBoringName

question.text: Given its flow meter's real state-dependent uncertainty `R(Q)`, does an active inference agent hold a centrifugal compressor's surge margin better than a fixed-margin anti-surge controller on the same plant? The example covers differential-pressure meters (orifice, venturi, nozzle) and Coriolis meters. "Better" is defined under the first result.

**The continuation is open as a paper. Lead authorship is yours of course. I'm happy to co-author the meter derivation and the cpomdp side if that helps and my contribution is sufficient. If not I only ask you cite cpomdp.**

firstResult.text: One meter type, Coriolis. The example covers it, and it is the case where the epistemic term pulls toward surge.

Give it a measured or literature-sourced uncertainty model, zero-stability term included. The SEVA work below reports an uncertainty with every measurement and is one place to start. Put a hard surge constraint on the margin. Run the agent and a fixed-margin anti-surge controller on the same plant, with the same meter and the same disturbances. Sweep `Λ` for the agent and the margin setting for the baseline, and report both margin-versus-efficiency curves. Efficiency here is recycle avoided.
"Better" means the agent's curve dominates. At the same rate of surge-limit violations it holds a smaller mean margin. Or at the same mean margin it violates less.
A negative result counts. An agent that needs the hard limit to stay out of surge, and does no better than a fixed margin once it has one, is worth writing up.

kind: Validation against a benchmark or oracle (RxInfer, published data)
status: Open, looking for someone to take it
